source_records.abstract: Purpose: Over 5M+ people in India rely on Indian Sign Language for communication with specially-abled people, and yet technological support remains very limited. We developed a real-time ISL recognition system as a proof-of-concept demonstrating CPU-based deployment feasibility. Methods: We adapted and optimized existing HWGAT architecture with 9.7M parameters (52.7% reduction from baseline) processing 29 MediaPipe-extracted keypoints enhanced with Fourier features, cyclic shifts, and learnable positional encodings. Our heuristic motion-gated mechanism uses simple displacement thresholds for continuous sign detection. Results: On a limited 6-class dataset (76 samples), the system achieved 78.57% validation accuracy. The 95% CI (49.2%-95.3%) reflects higher variance due to a small sample size, which indicates that the results should be interpreted as preliminary. Ablation studies show that incremental improvements are as such: learnable encodings (+8.33%), Fourier features (+7.14%), and cyclic shifts (+7.14%). Conclusion: Our work demonstrates the feasibility of a CPU-based ISL recognition but acknowledges its significant limitations: a small vocabulary, limited amount of training data and simpler motion-gating heuristics. Findings established baseline for future large-scale studies.

source_records.abstract: Spatial-temporal sequence forecasting (STSF) is a long-standing research problem with widespread real-world applications. The neural architecture search (NAS), which automates neural network design, is essential to adaptively model the correlated dependencies of spatial and temporal features for diverse downstream tasks in STSF. However, existing methods overlook the complex interaction between spatial and temporal operators, which causes a large number of irregular local optima obstructing both heuristic and gradient-based NAS methods. Despite the emerging LLM-based methods improve it with inner knowledge, there still lacks enough mechanism for memory and task decomposed instruction. In this paper, we propose a multilevel enhanced LLM-based NAS method for STSF. Instead of directly question-querying with LLM, we decompose the STSF NAS task into three levels, and inspire the LLM’s capability with an interactive multilevel enhancement mechanism. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves competitive effectiveness against 8 baselines in 5 datasets for STSF.

source_records.abstract: Existing multivariate time series anomaly detection methods are prone to interference from redundant channel noise in complex high-dimensional environments, leading to failure in spatial topology perception. To address this, we propose DCF-GSL, a spatio-temporal anomaly detection model based on dynamic channel fusion and graph structure learning. The model first captures multi-resolution temporal dependencies via multi-scale temporal convolutions. It then constructs a time-adaptive graph structure through learnable node embeddings and Top-K selection, mining local spatial correlations and global topological features by combining multi-head attention with topological persistent homology. A self-supervised masked attention mechanism with dynamic contrastive loss drives the model to actively learn complementary inter-channel relationships in latent space, adaptively filtering redundant noise and reinforcing key feature representations. Finally, a decoder predicts sensor values to generate normalized anomaly scores, and an adaptive thresholding strategy based on maximizing the F1-score enables precise detection. Experiments on SWaT, MSL, and SMD benchmarks demonstrate that DCF-GSL outperforms OmniAnomaly, GDN, TranAD, and other baselines in terms of F1-score.

source_records.abstract: State-of-health (SOH) assessment is essential for ensuring the reliability and safety of lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles. Traditional methods relying on time-series signals or handcrafted features often fail to capture complex degradation patterns across heterogeneous data modalities. We propose a multimodal SOH assessment framework that integrates electrochemical signals with pseudo-image representations generated by a generative adversarial network (GAN). An attention-guided fusion mechanism adaptively combines features from a CNN branch for images and an LSTM branch for temporal signals, enabling the model to focus on the most informative patterns. Experiments on multiple benchmark battery datasets show that our approach consistently surpasses unimodal and early-fusion baselines. On the XJTU battery dataset, it reduces the RMSE from 0.015722 to 0.006833 and improves R² from 0.888068 to 0.978852. This framework not only delivers accurate SOH estimation but also provides interpretable fusion of physical and visual indicators, offering a robust and generalizable solution for real-world battery prognostics.

source_records.abstract: Accurate and computationally efficient prediction of daily financial variables from accounting data is essential for practical industrial applications. In this study, we develop a predictive model based on an Echo State Network (ESN), a representative approach in reservoir computing, using real-world daily accounting datasets. For the task of predicting 31-day ahead cash balances and net working capital, the ESN outperforms the benchmark Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model by 1.324 percentage points in accuracy and surpasses the predictive performance reported in prior studies while achieving approximately 73 times faster training. Furthermore, we conduct a scenario analysis by feeding pseudo journal entries representing future scenarios into the model to examine changes in future financial variables. These results suggest that the ESN is a promising approach for structured accounting time series derived from double-entry bookkeeping, especially when the number of observations is limited, in terms of both predictive accuracy and training efficiency.

source_records.abstract: Spatio-temporal graph neural networks on directed heterogeneous graphs face two structural challenges: symmetric graph aggregations cannot distinguish directional propagation mechanisms, and pure likelihood-based density scoring can underweight sparse localized perturbations. We address both within DA-GTNF, a unified framework for freeway anomaly detection. First, a direction-aware heterogeneous graph explicitly encodes four asymmetric relation types (downstream propagation, upstream shockwave, lateral lane interaction, and diagonal lane change), enabling a Relational GCN to learn independent aggregation kernels per relation. Second, a DualBranchGating mechanism fuses spatial graph embeddings and temporal Transformer embeddings through adaptive, feature-wise gates derived from unfused outputs. Third, a Dual-Conditioned Normalizing Flow estimates exact token-wise conditional log-likelihoods of the gated embeddings, while an auxiliary reconstruction head improves sensitivity to micro-level deviations that may be weakly reflected by NLL alone. On FT-AED, DA-GTNF achieves an AUC of 0.7218, a Reporting Delay of −11.80 min, a Mean Localization Error of 2.23 miles, and 100% incident coverage. On PeMS with incomplete ground truth, the segment-level DA-GTNF variant also consistently improves Recall@K% over all compared baselines.

source_records.abstract: 3D skeleton-based gait emotion recognition faces high annotation costs, data scarcity, and poor generalization on heterogeneous data. This paper proposes SV-GCN, a single-stream multi-feature fusion framework with temporal invariance. We introduce intra-frame relative motion features to eliminate frame-rate sensitivity and embed heterogeneous cues at shallow layers, enabling early fusion without multi-stream complexity. For variable-length sequences, we design a global mask-guided valid-frame spatio-temporal graph convolution module, introducing frame-rate insensitivity for the first time in this domain. On the E-Gait dataset, our method achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art while demonstrating strong generalization across varying sequence lengths and frame rates, offering a viable pathway for pre-training on large-scale skeleton-based action recognition datasets. The code will be available at https://github.com/lsr51/SV-GCN .

source_records.abstract: The advancement of intelligent transportation systems (ITS) has necessitated the effective integration of diverse, multi-source traffic data. Conventional approaches reliant on singular structured data struggle to encapsulate the complementarity of diverse modal data, and therefore exhibit limits in intricate traffic environments. In recent years, the cross-modal fusion-based multi-modal knowledge representation learning (KRL) method has significantly improved the semantic depth and resilience of traffic entity representation by amalgamating text, images, time series, and structured graph data. This paper examines the current state of cross-modal data fusion in intelligent transportation, grounded in the theory of multi-source heterogeneous information and knowledge representation learning. It identifies existing technical challenges and explores future avenues for innovation, with the objective of establishing a novel approach to intelligent transportation control driven by KRL. Keywords: intelligent transportation management; knowledge representation learning; multi-source heterogeneous data; cross-modal data integration; massive language model.

source_records.abstract: Existing multivariate time series anomaly detection methods are prone to interference from redundant channel noise in complex high-dimensional environments, leading to failure in spatial topology perception. To address this, we propose DCF-GSL, a spatio-temporal anomaly detection model based on dynamic channel fusion and graph structure learning. The model first captures multi-resolution temporal dependencies via multi-scale temporal convolutions. It then constructs a time-adaptive graph structure through learnable node embeddings and Top-K selection, mining local spatial correlations and global topological features by combining multi-head attention with topological persistent homology. A self-supervised masked attention mechanism with dynamic contrastive loss drives the model to actively learn complementary inter-channel relationships in latent space, adaptively filtering redundant noise and reinforcing key feature representations. Finally, a decoder predicts sensor values to generate normalized anomaly scores, and an adaptive thresholding strategy based on maximizing the F1-score enables precise detection. Experiments on SWaT, MSL, and SMD benchmarks demonstrate that DCF-GSL outperforms OmniAnomaly, GDN, TranAD, and other baselines in terms of F1-score.

source_records.abstract: State-of-health (SOH) assessment is essential for ensuring the reliability and safety of lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles. Traditional methods relying on time-series signals or handcrafted features often fail to capture complex degradation patterns across heterogeneous data modalities. We propose a multimodal SOH assessment framework that integrates electrochemical signals with pseudo-image representations generated by a generative adversarial network (GAN). An attention-guided fusion mechanism adaptively combines features from a CNN branch for images and an LSTM branch for temporal signals, enabling the model to focus on the most informative patterns. Experiments on multiple benchmark battery datasets show that our approach consistently surpasses unimodal and early-fusion baselines. On the XJTU battery dataset, it reduces the RMSE from 0.015722 to 0.006833 and improves R² from 0.888068 to 0.978852. This framework not only delivers accurate SOH estimation but also provides interpretable fusion of physical and visual indicators, offering a robust and generalizable solution for real-world battery prognostics.

source_records.abstract: Accurate and computationally efficient prediction of daily financial variables from accounting data is essential for practical industrial applications. In this study, we develop a predictive model based on an Echo State Network (ESN), a representative approach in reservoir computing, using real-world daily accounting datasets. For the task of predicting 31-day ahead cash balances and net working capital, the ESN outperforms the benchmark Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model by 1.324 percentage points in accuracy and surpasses the predictive performance reported in prior studies while achieving approximately 73 times faster training. Furthermore, we conduct a scenario analysis by feeding pseudo journal entries representing future scenarios into the model to examine changes in future financial variables. These results suggest that the ESN is a promising approach for structured accounting time series derived from double-entry bookkeeping, especially when the number of observations is limited, in terms of both predictive accuracy and training efficiency.

source_records.abstract: Spatio-temporal graph neural networks on directed heterogeneous graphs face two structural challenges: symmetric graph aggregations cannot distinguish directional propagation mechanisms, and pure likelihood-based density scoring can underweight sparse localized perturbations. We address both within DA-GTNF, a unified framework for freeway anomaly detection. First, a direction-aware heterogeneous graph explicitly encodes four asymmetric relation types (downstream propagation, upstream shockwave, lateral lane interaction, and diagonal lane change), enabling a Relational GCN to learn independent aggregation kernels per relation. Second, a DualBranchGating mechanism fuses spatial graph embeddings and temporal Transformer embeddings through adaptive, feature-wise gates derived from unfused outputs. Third, a Dual-Conditioned Normalizing Flow estimates exact token-wise conditional log-likelihoods of the gated embeddings, while an auxiliary reconstruction head improves sensitivity to micro-level deviations that may be weakly reflected by NLL alone. On FT-AED, DA-GTNF achieves an AUC of 0.7218, a Reporting Delay of −11.80 min, a Mean Localization Error of 2.23 miles, and 100% incident coverage. On PeMS with incomplete ground truth, the segment-level DA-GTNF variant also consistently improves Recall@K% over all compared baselines.

source_records.abstract: 3D skeleton-based gait emotion recognition faces high annotation costs, data scarcity, and poor generalization on heterogeneous data. This paper proposes SV-GCN, a single-stream multi-feature fusion framework with temporal invariance. We introduce intra-frame relative motion features to eliminate frame-rate sensitivity and embed heterogeneous cues at shallow layers, enabling early fusion without multi-stream complexity. For variable-length sequences, we design a global mask-guided valid-frame spatio-temporal graph convolution module, introducing frame-rate insensitivity for the first time in this domain. On the E-Gait dataset, our method achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art while demonstrating strong generalization across varying sequence lengths and frame rates, offering a viable pathway for pre-training on large-scale skeleton-based action recognition datasets. The code will be available at https://github.com/lsr51/SV-GCN .

source_records.abstract: The advancement of intelligent transportation systems (ITS) has necessitated the effective integration of diverse, multi-source traffic data. Conventional approaches reliant on singular structured data struggle to encapsulate the complementarity of diverse modal data, and therefore exhibit limits in intricate traffic environments. In recent years, the cross-modal fusion-based multi-modal knowledge representation learning (KRL) method has significantly improved the semantic depth and resilience of traffic entity representation by amalgamating text, images, time series, and structured graph data. This paper examines the current state of cross-modal data fusion in intelligent transportation, grounded in the theory of multi-source heterogeneous information and knowledge representation learning. It identifies existing technical challenges and explores future avenues for innovation, with the objective of establishing a novel approach to intelligent transportation control driven by KRL. Keywords: intelligent transportation management; knowledge representation learning; multi-source heterogeneous data; cross-modal data integration; massive language model.
